1. packages/core/src/capability.ts:41 — `load()` deletes the whole preferences key whenever decoding fails (`kv.remove(Key)`) — a schema evolution or partially-written value then silently wipes every user preference on first read, irreversibly — don't destroy data you can't parse: log + ignore, or store a schema version alongside so migrations are possible.

2. packages/core/src/capability.ts:60 — `set()` does load → filter → write with no locking or serialization; two concurrent updates (two TUI clients, or rapid toggles from different surfaces than this dialog) lose one preference — wrap the read-modify-write in an Effect semaphore/single-flight like other config writers, since KV isn't transactional here.

3. packages/core/src/session/runner/to-llm-message.ts:227 + compaction.ts:141 — dropping `skills[].text` from message lowering and compaction means *pre-existing* sessions recorded with inline skill guidance lose that context when resumed or compacted after upgrade — fine as a forward-looking design, but worth a release note ("old sessions degrade to mention-only") and ideally a compaction fallback that re-resolves attachments by id if still installed.

4. packages/server/src/handlers/capability.ts:14 — `capability.list` calls `capability.get(ref)` per skill, and each `get` re-reads and re-decodes the entire preferences array from KV (O(N) reads per request) — load once and match locally, mirroring what the service already exposes via `list()`.

5. packages/core/test/capability.test.ts:8 — coverage of the happy path and inherit semantics is good, but the risky branches are untested: the corrupted-payload removal from item 1, concurrent `set` calls (item 2), and the new HTTP handler itself (list/update round-trip) — please pin down at least the first two before merge.

6. Nit — packages/tui/src/component/dialog-skill.tsx:47 — `toggle` derives the wire state as `preference ?? "inherit"` while optimistically rendering `state`; if another client flips `defaultState` between render and update, "inherit" lands on a different effective value than the checkbox showed — acceptable for a single-user dialog, just be aware the optimistic row can disagree until refresh.

Overall: nice abstraction — the Ref/Preference/Info split, event emission, and the move to on-demand skill loading via the tool are clean, and the TUI dialog rewrite (optimistic toggle + revert + search) is a clear UX win. Items 1–2 are the ones I'd fix pre-merge. Thanks!

1. packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts:99 — `foreignSchemaPassthrough` emits `Effect.logWarning` on **every execution** of every affected tool — a long-lived session calling an old-plugin tool hundreds of times floods logs with identical warnings — memoize the warning per schema/tool instance (a WeakSet/WeakMap keyed on the schema) so it logs once.

2. packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts:94 — `isForeignSchema` hinges on `schema.ast instanceof SchemaAST.Base`, i.e. an internal class identity of one specific effect build; an effect upgrade that restructures AST exports silently flips every schema to "foreign" (validation disabled for everyone), with only a warning as signal — add a guard test that pins this behavior against the bundled effect version, and document the invariant next to the check.

3. packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts:63 — the comment says "Array elements are positional and stay untouched", but the code maps `withoutNullProperties` over array items, which *does* strip null properties from objects inside arrays (only null *elements* survive) — the behavior looks right, the comment will mislead the next debugger; reword it.

4. packages/tui/src/context/local.tsx:236 — the default-model resource refetches only when `models()?.length` changes; a provider connecting while the catalog size happens to stay constant (swap, not grow) leaves the stale "No provider selected" state — consider keying on a catalog/provider revision event instead of the array length heuristic.

5. Nit — packages/plugin/src/effect/tool-schema.ts:31 — `Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(oriented as never)`: the double-`as never` casts hide real type constraints; if the converters' signatures tighten later this compiles anyway. A narrowly-typed helper would keep the compiler involved.

Overall: strong PR — the null-stripping retry preserves strict schemas (tests cover NullOr fields, arrays, and original-error reporting), the dual-effect-instance test fixture is exactly the right way to reproduce plugin isolation bugs, and the define()-time conversion fixes the root cause rather than the symptom. Items 1–2 are operational risks worth closing before merge. Thanks!

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

1. packages/cli/src/server-process.ts:48 — **ordering bug**: this finalizer is registered *first* in the scope, and Effect runs finalizers LIFO — so it executes **last**, after every other finalizer has already completed. A hung cleanup anywhere earlier in the teardown chain prevents this finalizer from ever running, so the watchdog never arms exactly in the scenario it exists for ("a finalizer never completes"). Arm the timer on scope *entry* instead (acquire-release style: start the unref'd timer before/at `Effect.scoped` entry, clear it in the `ensuring`) so it's live during the entire teardown window.

2. packages/cli/src/server-process.ts:52 — `process.exit(1)` gives zero diagnosis: consider writing one synchronous line to stderr ("shutdown exceeded 10s; forcing exit") before exiting, so users reporting "service wouldn't stop" have something to attach.

3. packages/cli/src/server-process.ts:45 — the `Set` holds exactly one timer for the lifetime of the effect; a plain `let watchdog` would do — and if item 1 is fixed by arming on entry, both the set and the per-mode branch simplify further.

4. Nit — packages/cli/src/server-process.ts:53 — 10s is hardcoded; fine as a default, but naming it (`SHUTDOWN_WATCHDOG_MS`) and colocating it with the other constants would make tuning discoverable. Also worth deciding whether non-service modes deserve the same bound, since a hung finalizer on Ctrl-C is equally annoying there.

Overall: right instinct — unbounded shutdown hangs are miserable to debug — but as written the guard fires only after every other finalizer succeeded, which misses the case it targets. Fixing the arming point makes this a genuinely valuable safety net. Thanks!

3. packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx:181/:196 — `(p as { state?: { status?: string } })` and `merged.push(req as never)` erode the type system exactly where correctness matters most (request shapes crossing a protocol boundary); the file already imports `QuestionRequest`/`PermissionRequest` — use them for the part-state narrowing too and drop the `as never`s by typing the merge helper once.
